is checking
had already checked
has already checked
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.

the result seemed doubtful
the planners revised their interpretation
questions.explanation: The people who performed the reviewing must immediately follow the opening modifier.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.

the previous chair
the original planners
the archive that stored the document
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: If Leena ___ responsible for the memorandum, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: is
were
will be
has been
questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: The memorandum may be accepted only if the planners approve it. What can be inferred?

No unapproved project has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
Their approval guarantees acceptance.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Leena as the person who actually inspected the evidence?

After she inspected it, Leena informed the chair.
The chair and Leena discussed the findings after she inspected it.
After inspecting the evidence, Leena informed the chair.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'After inspecting the evidence' directly modifies the named person who performed the inspection. The alternatives contain ambiguous pronouns or less clearly attach the action to its agent.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: Which sentence means that the planners revised no section except the conclusion?

Only the planners revised the conclusion of the memorandum.
The planners only revised the conclusion of the memorandum.
The planners revised the only conclusion of the memorandum.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The memorandum was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
The memorandum was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The memorandum was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The memorandum was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 4 archives full-paper case: The number of planners assigned to the task ___ increased since September.
options: were
are
has
have
questions.explanation: The singular head number takes has, despite the plural noun in its complement.

questions.text: The revised restoration report showed a decline in the number of sampling errors but also in the amount of sediment. Which pair of quantifiers correctly completes the sentence: 'There were ___ sampling errors and ___ sediment'?

less; less

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, A number of planners ___ raised concerns about the proposed interpretation.
options: have
has
is
was

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, Either the planners or the department head ___ required to approve the final memorandum.
options: have
is
are

questions.text: Which version correctly joins two complete observations about the wetland survey?

The ecologists recorded sampling errors: and heavy rainfall altered sampling.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, Which construction uses inversion correctly after the negative adverbial?

Not only did the jury revised its project but also explained.
Not only the jury had revised its project, but it also explaining.
Not only did the jury revise its project, but it also explained the change.
questions.explanation: Negative-initial not only requires auxiliary inversion in the first clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, Which version uses whose as a relative possessive rather than confusing it with who is?

The planner who's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The planner whose's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The planner who measurements were disputed requested a review.
questions.explanation: Whose is a possessive relative determiner; who's means who is or who has.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, Which sentence means that the director considered just one document and no others?

The director examined only the revised memorandum.
Only the director examined the revised memorandum.
The director only examined the revised memorandum.
questions.explanation: Only modifies the immediately following object 'the revised memorandum' to restrict the documents examined.

The habitat coverage of the wetland survey was higher than that of the older survey.
The habitat coverage of the wetland survey was higher than the authors of the older survey.
The habitat coverage of the wetland survey was more higher than the older survey.
questions.explanation: 'That of' substitutes for the corresponding measurement in the other project. The distractors compare unlike entities or use an ungrammatical double comparative.

questions.text: The team found a smaller quantity of sediment and a smaller number of sampling errors. Which sentence describes both changes with appropriate quantifiers?

The team recorded less sediment and fewer sampling errors.
The team recorded less sediment and less sampling errors.
The team recorded fewer sediment and fewer sampling errors.
questions.explanation: 'Less' modifies the uncountable quantity and 'fewer' modifies the countable plural. All other combinations misapply at least one quantifier.

questions.text: The river level ___ rapidly after the overnight storm.
options: rose
raised
risen
rising

questions.text: The team upheld the ethical ___ of informed consent.
options: principal
principle
precedent
principality
questions.explanation: A principle is a rule; principal means chief or main. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?

The editor said that the jury will have reviewed the evidence yesterday.
questions.explanation: Past reporting combines naturally with a past perfect for an earlier action.

Dr. Kim, who inspected the sensor array, submitted the findings.
Dr. Kim, who inspected the sensor array submitted the findings.
Dr. Kim who inspected the sensor array submitted, the findings.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, Which version makes the introductory action's agent unambiguous?

Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.
After studying the archive, a discrepancy appeared.
Having read the transcript, the memorandum's conclusions changed.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 environmental policy assessment, Which version appropriately uses were to express an unreal present condition?

The jury spoke as if the outcome were already certain.
The jury spoke as if the outcome will already certain.
The jury spoke as if the outcome had certain yesterday.

is
were
have

Whom was responsible for the analysis?

Whom did the panel invite to testify?

questions.text: Which version correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause explaining a decision about the wetland survey?

Although heavy rainfall altered sampling, the ecologists reviewed the evidence.
Although, heavy rainfall altered sampling the ecologists reviewed the evidence.
Although heavy rainfall altered sampling, and the ecologists reviewed the evidence.

The ecologists examined not only the field notebook but also that the restoration report was correct.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in native species observed but cannot separate wetland restoration from the competing circumstance that rainfall was unusually high during the trial. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?
options: The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
The positive change proves that every participant benefited exclusively from the program.
The competing circumstance disproves the existence of any possible program benefit.
No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: Which sentence maintains parallel structure and clearly assigns all three purposes to the same experiment?
options: The experiment was designed to estimate runoff, testing drainage, and whether vegetation could reduce erosion.
The experiment was designed to estimate runoff, test drainage, and determine whether vegetation could reduce erosion.
The experiment was designed for estimating runoff, to test drainage, and determine whether vegetation could reduce erosion.
The experiment was designed that runoff be estimated, testing drainage, and to determine vegetation.
questions.explanation: Three coordinated infinitives—estimate, test, and determine—follow 'designed to' and share a single subject.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: Each of the findings that the historians discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.
options: were
have been
is
are
questions.explanation: The singular distributive head each governs is despite the intervening plural phrase.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: By the time Dara presented the submission, the review team ___ its sources.
options: has already checked
will check
is checking
had already checked
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.

a discrepancy became apparent
the submission was amended

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.

that in the earlier submission
the previous chair
the original historians
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: If Dara ___ responsible for the submission, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: has been
is

questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: The submission may be accepted only if the historians approve it. What can be inferred?
options: Their approval guarantees acceptance.
Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
No unapproved draft has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Dara as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After inspecting the evidence, Dara informed the chair.
Dara informed the chair after she inspected it.
After she inspected it, Dara informed the chair.
The chair and Dara discussed the findings after she inspected it.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'After inspecting the evidence' directly modifies the named person who performed the inspection. The alternatives contain ambiguous pronouns or less clearly attach the action to its agent.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: Which sentence means that the historians revised no section except the conclusion?
options: The historians revised the only conclusion of the submission.
The historians revised only the conclusion of the submission.
Only the historians revised the conclusion of the submission.
The historians only revised the conclusion of the submission.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The submission was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
The submission was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
The submission was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The submission was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: The number of historians assigned to the task ___ increased since September.
options: have
were
are
has
questions.explanation: The singular head number takes has, despite the plural noun in its complement.

questions.text: The revised author correspondence showed a decline in the number of unsupported claims but also in the amount of ambiguity. Which pair of quantifiers correctly completes the sentence: 'There were ___ unsupported claims and ___ ambiguity'?
options: fewer; less
less; fewer
fewer; fewer
less; less

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, A number of historians ___ raised concerns about the proposed interpretation.

have
has

questions.explanation: A number of followed by a plural noun takes a plural verb.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Either the historians or the department head ___ required to approve the final submission.
options: were
have
is
are
questions.explanation: The nearest noun head is singular, so is is correct.

questions.text: Which version correctly joins two complete observations about the literary review?
options: The critics recorded unsupported claims; a chapter was omitted.
The critics recorded unsupported claims, a chapter was omitted.
The critics recorded unsupported claims; and, a chapter was omitted.
The critics recorded unsupported claims: and a chapter was omitted.
questions.explanation: The semicolon joins two related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction. The comma-only version splices clauses, while the other versions misuse punctuation with 'and'.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which construction uses inversion correctly after the negative adverbial?
options: Not only did the commission revise its draft, but it also explained the change.
Not only the commission did revise its draft, but explained also.
Not only did the commission revised its draft but also explained.
Not only the commission had revised its draft, but it also explaining.
questions.explanation: Negative-initial not only requires auxiliary inversion in the first clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which version uses whose as a relative possessive rather than confusing it with who is?
options: The historian who measurements were disputed requested a review.
The historian whose measurements were disputed requested a review.
The historian who's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The historian whose's measurements were disputed requested a review.
questions.explanation: Whose is a possessive relative determiner; who's means who is or who has.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which sentence means that the director considered just one document and no others?
options: The director only examined the revised submission.
The director examined the only revised submission.
The director examined only the revised submission.
Only the director examined the revised submission.
questions.explanation: Only modifies the immediately following object 'the revised submission' to restrict the documents examined.

questions.text: A report compares interpretive clarity in the literary review and the previous review. Which sentence correctly compares the measures rather than a measure with a project?
options: The interpretive clarity of the literary review was higher than that of the previous review.
The interpretive clarity of the literary review was higher than the previous review.
The interpretive clarity of the literary review was higher than the authors of the previous review.
The interpretive clarity of the literary review was more higher than the previous review.
questions.explanation: 'That of' substitutes for the corresponding measurement in the other project. The distractors compare unlike entities or use an ungrammatical double comparative.

questions.text: The team found a smaller quantity of ambiguity and a smaller number of unsupported claims. Which sentence describes both changes with appropriate quantifiers?
options: The team recorded less ambiguity and fewer unsupported claims.
The team recorded fewer ambiguity and less unsupported claims.
The team recorded less ambiguity and less unsupported claims.
The team recorded fewer ambiguity and fewer unsupported claims.
questions.explanation: 'Less' modifies the uncountable quantity and 'fewer' modifies the countable plural. All other combinations misapply at least one quantifier.

questions.text: Changing the final chapter may ___ readers' judgments about the narrator.
options: effect
affected
effected
affect
questions.explanation: Affect means influence and takes the base form after may; effect means bring about. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

questions.text: The reviewer asked the author to ___ the exact supporting study.
options: cite
site

questions.explanation: Cite means name a source as evidence; site and sight are different words. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?
options: The editor said that the commission will have reviewed the evidence yesterday.
The editor said that the commission review the evidence before it published.
The editor said that the commission had reviews the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the commission had reviewed the evidence before publishing.
questions.explanation: Past reporting combines naturally with a past perfect for an earlier action.

questions.text: The report has already identified Ms. Hart. Which sentence treats the additional information about this named person as nonessential?
options: Ms. Hart, who inspected the first edition, submitted the findings.
Ms. Hart who inspected the first edition, submitted the findings.
Ms. Hart, who inspected the first edition submitted the findings.
Ms. Hart who inspected the first edition submitted, the findings.
questions.explanation: A supplementary who-clause about an already identified person takes commas on both sides. The other versions omit or misplace a clause boundary.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which version makes the introductory action's agent unambiguous?

Having reviewed the transcript, the historian corrected the chronology.
Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.
After studying the archive, a discrepancy appeared.
questions.explanation: The historian is the following subject and therefore performs the reviewing.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which version appropriately uses were to express an unreal present condition?
options: The commission spoke as if the outcome had certain yesterday.

The commission spoke as if the outcome were already certain.
The commission spoke as if the outcome will already certain.
questions.explanation: Were marks a contrary-to-fact or hypothetical state in formal usage.

questions.text: Neither of the two interpretations offered for the literary review ___ supported by the available record. Which verb agrees with the singular distributive subject?

are

questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular in this formal construction, so it takes 'is' rather than a plural verb, regardless of the plural noun in the modifying phrase.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which question correctly uses whom in a formal object position?
options: Whom did the panel invite to testify?
Whom submitted the final submission?
Whom was responsible for the analysis?
Whom have been approved for the hearing?
questions.explanation: Whom is the object of invite; the other questions need subject-case who.

questions.text: Which version correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause explaining a decision about the literary review?
options: Although a chapter was omitted, the critics reviewed the evidence.
Although a chapter was omitted the critics, reviewed the evidence.
Although, a chapter was omitted the critics reviewed the evidence.
Although a chapter was omitted, and the critics reviewed the evidence.
questions.explanation: The initial subordinate clause is followed by a comma before the main clause. The other choices misplace the comma or add an ungrammatical conjunction.

questions.text: Which sentence uses parallel objects after 'not only ... but also' when describing the literary review?
options: The critics examined not only the draft preface but also the author correspondence.
The critics examined not only the draft preface but also analyzing the author correspondence.
The critics examined not only the draft preface but also to evaluate the author correspondence.
The critics examined not only the draft preface but also that the author correspondence was correct.
questions.explanation: Both objects are parallel noun phrases governed by 'examined'. The alternatives shift to a participial, infinitival, or finite clause complement.

questions.text: A district compared average exam scores before and after changing a curriculum, but the tested cohorts were different. Which statement is strongest?
options: The curriculum caused the difference because averages are objective.
The cohort difference prevents a straightforward causal attribution without further analysis.
The comparison cannot show that scores changed.
Every student in the later cohort must have improved.
questions.explanation: A cohort shift may affect the average independently of teaching changes. The mean difference is real but its cause is not established.

questions.text: A clinic claims that a new appointment reminder system reduced missed visits. Which comparison most directly tests that claim?
options: Patient satisfaction after the change alone.
Missed-visit rates for similar appointment groups with and without reminders over comparable periods.
A count of reminders sent in the first week.
A testimonial from a patient who likes notifications.
questions.explanation: Comparable no-show rates with a relevant control group target the effect while accounting for differences between patient groups and periods.

questions.text: A proposal to expand a school reading club faces this objection: the club uses time from other enrichment activities. Which response keeps a defensible argument without dismissing the concern?
options: Although the club uses time from other enrichment activities, a restricted pilot that measures reading-comprehension results could show whether expansion is justified.
The expense matters, but a school reading club has already been discussed widely enough that measuring outcomes is unnecessary.
Because the program is intended to help, its costs and risks should not be weighed in the decision.
The concern could be reduced by delaying the decision, even if the program's effect on reading-comprehension results is never measured.
questions.explanation: The strongest response acknowledges the specific burden while proposing evidence about reading-comprehension results. The alternatives appeal to publicity, intentions, or postponement without addressing effectiveness and cost together.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in robotics?
options: Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: A paragraph reports encouraging initial results for a school reading club. The next explains that participating students already read more before joining. Which transition and qualification best connect the paragraphs?
options: Furthermore, the timing of the competing change demonstrates that the new program produced the entire benefit.
By contrast, the competing change establishes that the program had no effect at all.
Nevertheless, participating students already read more before joining, so the effect of the program itself remains uncertain.
Consequently, additional evidence is unnecessary because both changes occurred in the same period.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' marks a limitation to positive findings and preserves uncertainty about the competing change. The other options assert proof of benefit or ineffectiveness or dismiss the need for comparison.

questions.text: In the day 5 robotics full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in robotics?
options: Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?
options: All respondents prefer answering surveys.
The survey submission contains at least two paragraphs.
The historians interviewed every official.
The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: Observed reading-comprehension results changed after a school reading club began. At the same time, participating students already read more before joining. Which interpretation avoids a post hoc fallacy?
options: Any favorable change following the launch must have resulted from the program.
The concurrent change proves the program was irrelevant in every setting.
Since both changes occurred together, they must have had exactly equal effects.
The timing is compatible with an effect, but it cannot isolate the program from the concurrent change.
questions.explanation: The observation alone cannot separate simultaneous causes. The first interpretation preserves the association while recognizing the alternate explanation; the other options infer necessity, absence, or equal effects without evidence.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: The cost is irrelevant because the draft is well intentioned.
Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: A critic says a school reading club may have uncertain effects because participating students already read more before joining. Which reply avoids misrepresenting the objection?
options: The critic believes every program should be banned permanently.
The critic rejects all evidence that could ever support the program.
The objection concerns the ability to separate causes, so we should measure the competing change before drawing conclusions.
The critic is opposed to helping the people served by the program.
questions.explanation: The correct response answers the actual causal concern. The alternatives substitute extreme claims about the critic's values or beliefs.

questions.text: A council attributes changes in reading-comprehension results to a school reading club. Which evidence would most directly evaluate this causal claim?
options: Comparable before-and-after outcome measures, with baseline differences and participating students already read more before joining accounted for.
The number of promotional materials distributed when the project started.
An opinion survey among only those who chose to enroll after the announcement.
A count of project meetings, without any recorded reading-comprehension results.
questions.explanation: Outcome measures with appropriate comparison and confounder accounting directly address the alleged improvement. Promotion, selective opinions and meeting totals are weak substitutes for the claimed outcome.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 literary criticism assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
A larger poster advertising the first trial.
An additional summary of the same initial observations.
Removing participants who disagree with the historian's conclusion.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: One paragraph reports encouraging changes in reading-comprehension results; the next considers participating students already read more before joining. Which opening makes the relationship clear?
options: Furthermore, the competing circumstance demonstrates the program was the sole cause.
Nevertheless, the competing circumstance limits any immediate claim that the program alone caused the improvement.
Similarly, the complication proves every finding is false.
Therefore, causal uncertainty can be ignored because the outcome was favorable.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a qualification to favorable evidence and states what remains uncertain. The other transitions turn concurrent changes into unjustified proof.

questions.text: A student is writing a policy essay about a school reading club. Which thesis is both contestable and specific enough to evaluate?
options: There are many views about the program, some supportive and some critical.
A limited expansion should be considered if measured gains in reading-comprehension results justify costs after accounting for competing explanations.
This essay will discuss several possible aspects of the proposed program.
The program is good because well-intentioned people have recommended it.
questions.explanation: The first thesis advocates a concrete conditional policy grounded in outcomes and costs. The other statements merely announce a topic, summarize opinions, or rely on intentions rather than evaluable reasoning.

questions.text: Two explanations fit an observed shift in reading-comprehension results: the launch of a school reading club and the fact that participating students already read more before joining. Which next measurement best distinguishes them?
options: Compare similar groups with differing exposure to the program while measuring the competing change.
Collect additional testimonials from people who already believe the program worked.
Repeat the preferred explanation in the report's conclusion.
Measure the launch date more precisely without collecting any outcome data.
questions.explanation: A comparison varying exposure while tracking the rival factor tests divergent causal predictions. Testimonials, repetition and precise launch dates alone do not discriminate explanations.

questions.text: A review seeks to estimate whether a school reading club altered reading-comprehension results. Which approach supplies the most defensible counterfactual?
options: Compare the participants' comments only after the program has ended.
Use the program's stated objective as evidence that it reached that objective.
Measure only the most successful pilot site and generalize to every site.
Compare suitably matched participants or sites with and without the program, adjusting for baseline outcome differences.
questions.explanation: A matched comparison with baseline adjustment can approximate what would have happened without the intervention. Selection based on success and opinions or intentions cannot establish the counterfactual.

questions.text: A sponsor claims a school reading club produced a lasting improvement in reading-comprehension results. Which assessment most fairly evaluates the sponsor's evidence?
options: Accept the claim if the sponsor has a prestigious professional title.
Reject the claim without examination because the source has a financial interest.
Inspect the sampling method, underlying outcome data, and independent replication while checking the competing change.
Count how many different websites repeat the sponsor's press release.
questions.explanation: Evaluating methods, records and independent evidence addresses both credibility and possible bias. Reputation, automatic dismissal, and repetitive citation alone are not sufficient tests.

questions.text: An archived local report describes a school reading club at one site in a particular year. Which historical inference is warranted without additional records?
options: The program must have been identical at every institution in the country.
The program was documented at that site, but its prevalence or effects elsewhere remain uncertain.
The archived description proves every participant supported the program.
The presence of one report establishes its effectiveness throughout the entire period.
questions.explanation: One record can document existence in its own context but cannot establish geographic prevalence, universal attitudes, or effectiveness without corroboration.

questions.text: A writer compares an initial pilot of a school reading club with a trial of a new school schedule. When would the analogy offer meaningful evidence for expansion?
options: When both pilots share relevant constraints, comparable target groups, and outcomes measured against plausible alternatives.
When both initiatives were announced in the same season, regardless of their mechanisms.
When their titles sound similar even if the intended users differ.
When the school trial was popular, even if it never measured any outcome.
questions.explanation: Analogies support inference when the features bearing on the conclusion are shared. Superficial timing, naming, and popularity do not establish comparable mechanisms or outcomes.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in reading-comprehension results but cannot separate a school reading club from the competing circumstance that participating students already read more before joining. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?

No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: Which revision makes it clear that the coach, not the team captain, had questioned the strategy?

questions.text: A report compares student engagement in the school pilot and the earlier pilot. Which sentence correctly compares the measures rather than a measure with a project?

The student engagement of the school pilot was higher than that of the earlier pilot.
questions.explanation: 'That of' substitutes for the corresponding measurement in the other project. The distractors compare unlike entities or use an ungrammatical double comparative.

questions.text: The team found a smaller quantity of uncertainty and a smaller number of attendance errors. Which sentence describes both changes with appropriate quantifiers?

The team recorded fewer uncertainty and fewer attendance errors.
The team recorded less uncertainty and fewer attendance errors.

questions.text: Before class, the teacher ___ the worksheets on each desk.

questions.text: The counselor handled confidential records with professional ___.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 educational policy assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?

Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 educational policy assessment, Which question correctly uses whom in a formal object position?

questions.text: An editorial supports protected bicycle lanes but acknowledges reduced curbside parking. Which sentence provides the most relevant rebuttal?

questions.text: Students using a new writing app revise their essays more often. What additional measure best assesses whether the app improves writing quality rather than mere editing activity?

How much students enjoy the app's colors.
questions.explanation: Revision frequency measures behavior, but blinded writing-quality ratings directly assess the educational outcome.

questions.text: A proposal to expand after-school mathematics tutoring faces this objection: additional tutors strain the school budget. Which response keeps a defensible argument without dismissing the concern?

Because the program is intended to help, its costs and risks should not be weighed in the decision.
The concern could be reduced by delaying the decision, even if the program's effect on improvement in reasoning scores is never measured.
Although additional tutors strain the school budget, a restricted pilot that measures improvement in reasoning scores could show whether expansion is justified.
questions.explanation: The strongest response acknowledges the specific burden while proposing evidence about improvement in reasoning scores. The alternatives appeal to publicity, intentions, or postponement without addressing effectiveness and cost together.

questions.text: In the day 6 ethics full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in ethics?
options: Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: A paragraph reports encouraging initial results for after-school mathematics tutoring. The next explains that the school also adopted a new textbook. Which transition and qualification best connect the paragraphs?
options: Furthermore, the timing of the competing change demonstrates that the new program produced the entire benefit.
Nevertheless, the school also adopted a new textbook, so the effect of the program itself remains uncertain.
By contrast, the competing change establishes that the program had no effect at all.
Consequently, additional evidence is unnecessary because both changes occurred in the same period.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' marks a limitation to positive findings and preserves uncertainty about the competing change. The other options assert proof of benefit or ineffectiveness or dismiss the need for comparison.

questions.text: In the day 6 ethics full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in ethics?
options: The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 educational policy assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?

The survey account contains at least two paragraphs.
The consultants interviewed every official.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: Observed improvement in reasoning scores changed after after-school mathematics tutoring began. At the same time, the school also adopted a new textbook. Which interpretation avoids a post hoc fallacy?
options: Any favorable change following the launch must have resulted from the program.
The concurrent change proves the program was irrelevant in every setting.
The timing is compatible with an effect, but it cannot isolate the program from the concurrent change.
Since both changes occurred together, they must have had exactly equal effects.
questions.explanation: The observation alone cannot separate simultaneous causes. The first interpretation preserves the association while recognizing the alternate explanation; the other options infer necessity, absence, or equal effects without evidence.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 educational policy assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
The cost is irrelevant because the scheme is well intentioned.
Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: A critic says after-school mathematics tutoring may have uncertain effects because the school also adopted a new textbook. Which reply avoids misrepresenting the objection?
options: The critic believes every program should be banned permanently.
The critic rejects all evidence that could ever support the program.
The critic is opposed to helping the people served by the program.
The objection concerns the ability to separate causes, so we should measure the competing change before drawing conclusions.
questions.explanation: The correct response answers the actual causal concern. The alternatives substitute extreme claims about the critic's values or beliefs.

questions.text: A council attributes changes in improvement in reasoning scores to after-school mathematics tutoring. Which evidence would most directly evaluate this causal claim?
options: The number of promotional materials distributed when the project started.
An opinion survey among only those who chose to enroll after the announcement.
A count of project meetings, without any recorded improvement in reasoning scores.
Comparable before-and-after outcome measures, with baseline differences and the school also adopted a new textbook accounted for.
questions.explanation: Outcome measures with appropriate comparison and confounder accounting directly address the alleged improvement. Promotion, selective opinions and meeting totals are weak substitutes for the claimed outcome.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 educational policy assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: Removing participants who disagree with the consultant's conclusion.
Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
A larger poster advertising the first trial.
An additional summary of the same initial observations.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: One paragraph reports encouraging changes in improvement in reasoning scores; the next considers the school also adopted a new textbook. Which opening makes the relationship clear?
options: Furthermore, the competing circumstance demonstrates the program was the sole cause.
Similarly, the complication proves every finding is false.
Nevertheless, the competing circumstance limits any immediate claim that the program alone caused the improvement.
Therefore, causal uncertainty can be ignored because the outcome was favorable.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a qualification to favorable evidence and states what remains uncertain. The other transitions turn concurrent changes into unjustified proof.

questions.text: A student is writing a policy essay about after-school mathematics tutoring. Which thesis is both contestable and specific enough to evaluate?
options: A limited expansion should be considered if measured gains in improvement in reasoning scores justify costs after accounting for competing explanations.
There are many views about the program, some supportive and some critical.
This essay will discuss several possible aspects of the proposed program.
The program is good because well-intentioned people have recommended it.
questions.explanation: The first thesis advocates a concrete conditional policy grounded in outcomes and costs. The other statements merely announce a topic, summarize opinions, or rely on intentions rather than evaluable reasoning.

questions.text: Two explanations fit an observed shift in improvement in reasoning scores: the launch of after-school mathematics tutoring and the fact that the school also adopted a new textbook. Which next measurement best distinguishes them?
options: Collect additional testimonials from people who already believe the program worked.
Repeat the preferred explanation in the report's conclusion.
Measure the launch date more precisely without collecting any outcome data.
Compare similar groups with differing exposure to the program while measuring the competing change.
questions.explanation: A comparison varying exposure while tracking the rival factor tests divergent causal predictions. Testimonials, repetition and precise launch dates alone do not discriminate explanations.

questions.text: A review seeks to estimate whether after-school mathematics tutoring altered improvement in reasoning scores. Which approach supplies the most defensible counterfactual?
options: Compare the participants' comments only after the program has ended.
Use the program's stated objective as evidence that it reached that objective.
Compare suitably matched participants or sites with and without the program, adjusting for baseline outcome differences.
Measure only the most successful pilot site and generalize to every site.
questions.explanation: A matched comparison with baseline adjustment can approximate what would have happened without the intervention. Selection based on success and opinions or intentions cannot establish the counterfactual.

questions.text: A sponsor claims after-school mathematics tutoring produced a lasting improvement in improvement in reasoning scores. Which assessment most fairly evaluates the sponsor's evidence?
options: Accept the claim if the sponsor has a prestigious professional title.
Inspect the sampling method, underlying outcome data, and independent replication while checking the competing change.
Reject the claim without examination because the source has a financial interest.
Count how many different websites repeat the sponsor's press release.
questions.explanation: Evaluating methods, records and independent evidence addresses both credibility and possible bias. Reputation, automatic dismissal, and repetitive citation alone are not sufficient tests.

questions.text: An archived local report describes after-school mathematics tutoring at one site in a particular year. Which historical inference is warranted without additional records?
options: The program was documented at that site, but its prevalence or effects elsewhere remain uncertain.
The program must have been identical at every institution in the country.
The archived description proves every participant supported the program.
The presence of one report establishes its effectiveness throughout the entire period.
questions.explanation: One record can document existence in its own context but cannot establish geographic prevalence, universal attitudes, or effectiveness without corroboration.

questions.text: A writer compares an initial pilot of after-school mathematics tutoring with a trial of a new school schedule. When would the analogy offer meaningful evidence for expansion?
options: When both initiatives were announced in the same season, regardless of their mechanisms.
When their titles sound similar even if the intended users differ.
When the school trial was popular, even if it never measured any outcome.
When both pilots share relevant constraints, comparable target groups, and outcomes measured against plausible alternatives.
questions.explanation: Analogies support inference when the features bearing on the conclusion are shared. Superficial timing, naming, and popularity do not establish comparable mechanisms or outcomes.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in improvement in reasoning scores but cannot separate after-school mathematics tutoring from the competing circumstance that the school also adopted a new textbook. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?
options: The positive change proves that every participant benefited exclusively from the program.
The competing circumstance disproves the existence of any possible program benefit.
The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: If the archive ___ able to confirm the letter's date, its curator ___ revise the disputed label; the evidence, however, remains inconclusive.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: The document may be accepted only if the scientists approve it. What can be inferred?

questions.text: Which word is misspelled?

questions.text: A nutrition study found an association between a dietary pattern and lower illness rates after accounting for age, but not physical activity. Which claim fits the evidence?
options: The association remained after age adjustment, but unmeasured exercise differences could still influence it.
The diet necessarily prevents illness in every age group.
Adjusting for age eliminates all confounding variables.
The findings are meaningless because exercise was not controlled.
questions.explanation: Age adjustment reduces one concern but does not eliminate confounding from omitted activity; the finding is suggestive, not universal or worthless.

questions.text: A city measures shorter bus travel times only on routes with dedicated lanes after construction. Which comparison would best identify the lanes' contribution?
options: Peak-hour bus travel times on similar routes without new lanes, measured before and after the change.
The number of buses manufactured that year.
An interview with the road contractor.
Passenger opinions about bus paint colors.
questions.explanation: A before-after comparison with unaffected routes helps separate lane effects from wider traffic trends.

questions.text: A proposal to expand adaptive traffic signals faces this objection: installation disrupts nearby businesses. Which response keeps a defensible argument without dismissing the concern?
options: The expense matters, but adaptive traffic signals has already been discussed widely enough that measuring outcomes is unnecessary.
Because the program is intended to help, its costs and risks should not be weighed in the decision.
Although installation disrupts nearby businesses, a restricted pilot that measures intersection delay times could show whether expansion is justified.
The concern could be reduced by delaying the decision, even if the program's effect on intersection delay times is never measured.
questions.explanation: The strongest response acknowledges the specific burden while proposing evidence about intersection delay times. The alternatives appeal to publicity, intentions, or postponement without addressing effectiveness and cost together.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in ecology?
options: Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: A paragraph reports encouraging initial results for adaptive traffic signals. The next explains that regional traffic declined during construction. Which transition and qualification best connect the paragraphs?
options: Nevertheless, regional traffic declined during construction, so the effect of the program itself remains uncertain.
Furthermore, the timing of the competing change demonstrates that the new program produced the entire benefit.
By contrast, the competing change establishes that the program had no effect at all.
Consequently, additional evidence is unnecessary because both changes occurred in the same period.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' marks a limitation to positive findings and preserves uncertainty about the competing change. The other options assert proof of benefit or ineffectiveness or dismiss the need for comparison.

questions.text: In the day 7 ecology full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in ecology?
options: An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 civic administration assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?
options: The scientists interviewed every official.
The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
All respondents prefer answering surveys.
The survey document contains at least two paragraphs.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: Observed intersection delay times changed after adaptive traffic signals began. At the same time, regional traffic declined during construction. Which interpretation avoids a post hoc fallacy?
options: Any favorable change following the launch must have resulted from the program.
The timing is compatible with an effect, but it cannot isolate the program from the concurrent change.
The concurrent change proves the program was irrelevant in every setting.
Since both changes occurred together, they must have had exactly equal effects.
questions.explanation: The observation alone cannot separate simultaneous causes. The first interpretation preserves the association while recognizing the alternate explanation; the other options infer necessity, absence, or equal effects without evidence.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 civic administration assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
The cost is irrelevant because the measure is well intentioned.
Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 civic administration assessment, Which sentence avoids a straw-man response?
options: The objection concerns uncertainty in the sample, which the next program should directly address.
The critic believes no data should ever be collected.
The critic must oppose every form of scientific inquiry.
The objection is false because the critic sounds worried.
questions.explanation: A fair rebuttal answers the actual concern about sampling rather than misrepresenting it as total opposition.

questions.text: A council attributes changes in intersection delay times to adaptive traffic signals. Which evidence would most directly evaluate this causal claim?
options: The number of promotional materials distributed when the project started.
An opinion survey among only those who chose to enroll after the announcement.
Comparable before-and-after outcome measures, with baseline differences and regional traffic declined during construction accounted for.
A count of project meetings, without any recorded intersection delay times.
questions.explanation: Outcome measures with appropriate comparison and confounder accounting directly address the alleged improvement. Promotion, selective opinions and meeting totals are weak substitutes for the claimed outcome.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 civic administration assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: An additional summary of the same initial observations.
Removing participants who disagree with the scientist's conclusion.
Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
A larger poster advertising the first trial.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 civic administration assessment, Which transition links a paragraph of favorable evidence to a paragraph about its limits?
options: Consequently, all uncertainty has disappeared.
For instance, the first result proves every outcome.
Likewise, no further evidence is needed.
Nevertheless, the program's restricted time frame prevents stronger conclusions.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals a contrast between encouraging findings and a meaningful qualification.

questions.text: A student is writing a policy essay about adaptive traffic signals. Which thesis is both contestable and specific enough to evaluate?
options: There are many views about the program, some supportive and some critical.
This essay will discuss several possible aspects of the proposed program.
The program is good because well-intentioned people have recommended it.
A limited expansion should be considered if measured gains in intersection delay times justify costs after accounting for competing explanations.
questions.explanation: The first thesis advocates a concrete conditional policy grounded in outcomes and costs. The other statements merely announce a topic, summarize opinions, or rely on intentions rather than evaluable reasoning.

questions.text: Two explanations fit an observed shift in intersection delay times: the launch of adaptive traffic signals and the fact that regional traffic declined during construction. Which next measurement best distinguishes them?
options: Collect additional testimonials from people who already believe the program worked.
Repeat the preferred explanation in the report's conclusion.
Compare similar groups with differing exposure to the program while measuring the competing change.
Measure the launch date more precisely without collecting any outcome data.
questions.explanation: A comparison varying exposure while tracking the rival factor tests divergent causal predictions. Testimonials, repetition and precise launch dates alone do not discriminate explanations.

questions.text: A review seeks to estimate whether adaptive traffic signals altered intersection delay times. Which approach supplies the most defensible counterfactual?
options: Compare the participants' comments only after the program has ended.
Compare suitably matched participants or sites with and without the program, adjusting for baseline outcome differences.
Use the program's stated objective as evidence that it reached that objective.
Measure only the most successful pilot site and generalize to every site.
questions.explanation: A matched comparison with baseline adjustment can approximate what would have happened without the intervention. Selection based on success and opinions or intentions cannot establish the counterfactual.

questions.text: A sponsor claims adaptive traffic signals produced a lasting improvement in intersection delay times. Which assessment most fairly evaluates the sponsor's evidence?
options: Inspect the sampling method, underlying outcome data, and independent replication while checking the competing change.
Accept the claim if the sponsor has a prestigious professional title.
Reject the claim without examination because the source has a financial interest.
Count how many different websites repeat the sponsor's press release.
questions.explanation: Evaluating methods, records and independent evidence addresses both credibility and possible bias. Reputation, automatic dismissal, and repetitive citation alone are not sufficient tests.

questions.text: An archived local report describes adaptive traffic signals at one site in a particular year. Which historical inference is warranted without additional records?
options: The program must have been identical at every institution in the country.
The archived description proves every participant supported the program.
The presence of one report establishes its effectiveness throughout the entire period.
The program was documented at that site, but its prevalence or effects elsewhere remain uncertain.
questions.explanation: One record can document existence in its own context but cannot establish geographic prevalence, universal attitudes, or effectiveness without corroboration.

questions.text: A writer compares an initial pilot of adaptive traffic signals with a trial of a new school schedule. When would the analogy offer meaningful evidence for expansion?
options: When both initiatives were announced in the same season, regardless of their mechanisms.
When their titles sound similar even if the intended users differ.
When both pilots share relevant constraints, comparable target groups, and outcomes measured against plausible alternatives.
When the school trial was popular, even if it never measured any outcome.
questions.explanation: Analogies support inference when the features bearing on the conclusion are shared. Superficial timing, naming, and popularity do not establish comparable mechanisms or outcomes.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in intersection delay times but cannot separate adaptive traffic signals from the competing circumstance that regional traffic declined during construction. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?
options: The positive change proves that every participant benefited exclusively from the program.
The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
The competing circumstance disproves the existence of any possible program benefit.
No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly punctuates a contrast between two independent clauses?
options: The proposed method was inexpensive, nevertheless, it had not been validated.
The proposed method was inexpensive; nevertheless, it had not been validated.
The proposed method was inexpensive; nevertheless it had not, been validated.
The proposed method was inexpensive nevertheless; it had not been validated.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates two independent clauses, and a comma follows the conjunctive adverb 'nevertheless'.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Each of the findings that the surveyors discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.

is
are
were

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: By the time Tara presented the paper, the review team ___ its sources.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.

the previous chair
the original surveyors
the archive that stored the document

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: If Tara ___ responsible for the paper, the chair would seek independent confirmation.

were

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: The paper may be accepted only if the surveyors approve it. What can be inferred?

No unapproved recommendation has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
Their approval guarantees acceptance.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Tara as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: Tara informed the chair after she inspected it.
After she inspected it, Tara informed the chair.
The chair and Tara discussed the findings after she inspected it.
After inspecting the evidence, Tara informed the chair.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'After inspecting the evidence' directly modifies the named person who performed the inspection. The alternatives contain ambiguous pronouns or less clearly attach the action to its agent.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Which sentence means that the surveyors revised no section except the conclusion?
options: The surveyors revised only the conclusion of the paper.
Only the surveyors revised the conclusion of the paper.
The surveyors only revised the conclusion of the paper.
The surveyors revised the only conclusion of the paper.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?

The paper was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The paper was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The paper was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 8 civic planning full-paper case: The number of surveyors assigned to the task ___ increased since September.

The inspectors recorded sorting mistakes: and the depot changed its hours.

The surveyor who measurements were disputed requested a review.

The collection efficiency of the recycling program was higher than that of the old program.
The collection efficiency of the recycling program was higher than the authors of the old program.
The collection efficiency of the recycling program was more higher than the old program.

questions.text: The team found a smaller quantity of waste and a smaller number of sorting mistakes. Which sentence describes both changes with appropriate quantifiers?

The team recorded less waste and fewer sorting mistakes.
The team recorded less waste and less sorting mistakes.
The team recorded fewer waste and fewer sorting mistakes.
questions.explanation: 'Less' modifies the uncountable quantity and 'fewer' modifies the countable plural. All other combinations misapply at least one quantifier.

questions.text: The volume recycled has ___ steadily since the new depot opened.

Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.

Having read the transcript, the paper's conclusions changed.
