questions.text: A review seeks to estimate whether household recycling incentives altered the share of household waste recycled. Which approach supplies the most defensible counterfactual?
options: Compare suitably matched participants or sites with and without the program, adjusting for baseline outcome differences.
Compare the participants' comments only after the program has ended.
Use the program's stated objective as evidence that it reached that objective.
Measure only the most successful pilot site and generalize to every site.
questions.explanation: A matched comparison with baseline adjustment can approximate what would have happened without the intervention. Selection based on success and opinions or intentions cannot establish the counterfactual.

questions.text: A sponsor claims household recycling incentives produced a lasting improvement in the share of household waste recycled. Which assessment most fairly evaluates the sponsor's evidence?
options: Accept the claim if the sponsor has a prestigious professional title.
Reject the claim without examination because the source has a financial interest.
Count how many different websites repeat the sponsor's press release.
Inspect the sampling method, underlying outcome data, and independent replication while checking the competing change.
questions.explanation: Evaluating methods, records and independent evidence addresses both credibility and possible bias. Reputation, automatic dismissal, and repetitive citation alone are not sufficient tests.

questions.text: An archived local report describes household recycling incentives at one site in a particular year. Which historical inference is warranted without additional records?
options: The program must have been identical at every institution in the country.
The archived description proves every participant supported the program.
The program was documented at that site, but its prevalence or effects elsewhere remain uncertain.
The presence of one report establishes its effectiveness throughout the entire period.
questions.explanation: One record can document existence in its own context but cannot establish geographic prevalence, universal attitudes, or effectiveness without corroboration.

questions.text: A writer compares an initial pilot of household recycling incentives with a trial of a new school schedule. When would the analogy offer meaningful evidence for expansion?
options: When both initiatives were announced in the same season, regardless of their mechanisms.
When both pilots share relevant constraints, comparable target groups, and outcomes measured against plausible alternatives.
When their titles sound similar even if the intended users differ.
When the school trial was popular, even if it never measured any outcome.
questions.explanation: Analogies support inference when the features bearing on the conclusion are shared. Superficial timing, naming, and popularity do not establish comparable mechanisms or outcomes.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in the share of household waste recycled but cannot separate household recycling incentives from the competing circumstance that a new recycling depot opened that month. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?
options: The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
The positive change proves that every participant benefited exclusively from the program.
The competing circumstance disproves the existence of any possible program benefit.
No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: Which sentence compares like quantities without introducing ambiguity about what increased?
options: Rainfall in June was higher than the preceding year.
Rainfall in June was higher than May did.
June's recorded rainfall was higher than that recorded in May.
June's rainfall was higher than the weather station.
questions.explanation: 'That recorded in May' makes clear that two rainfall totals, rather than months, a year or an instrument, are being compared.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: Each of the findings that the scholars discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.
options: were
have been
is
are
questions.explanation: The singular distributive head each governs is despite the intervening plural phrase.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: By the time Ravi presented the summary, the review team ___ its sources.
options: has already checked
will check
is checking
had already checked
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.
options: the scholars revised their interpretation
a discrepancy became apparent
the summary was amended
the result seemed doubtful
questions.explanation: The people who performed the reviewing must immediately follow the opening modifier.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.
options: the archive that stored the document
that in the earlier summary
the previous chair
the original scholars
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: If Ravi ___ responsible for the summary, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: has been
is
were
will be
questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: The summary may be accepted only if the scholars approve it. What can be inferred?
options: Their approval guarantees acceptance.
Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
No unapproved policy has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Ravi as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After inspecting the evidence, Ravi informed the chair.
Ravi informed the chair after she inspected it.
After she inspected it, Ravi informed the chair.
The chair and Ravi discussed the findings after she inspected it.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'After inspecting the evidence' directly modifies the named person who performed the inspection. The alternatives contain ambiguous pronouns or less clearly attach the action to its agent.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: Which sentence means that the scholars revised no section except the conclusion?
options: The scholars revised the only conclusion of the summary.
The scholars revised only the conclusion of the summary.
Only the scholars revised the conclusion of the summary.
The scholars only revised the conclusion of the summary.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The summary was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
The summary was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
The summary was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The summary was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 9 linguistics full-paper case: The number of scholars assigned to the task ___ increased since September.
options: have
were
are
has
questions.explanation: The singular head number takes has, despite the plural noun in its complement.

questions.text: The revised accessibility review showed a decline in the number of entry delays but also in the amount of uncertainty. Which pair of quantifiers correctly completes the sentence: 'There were ___ entry delays and ___ uncertainty'?
options: fewer; less
less; fewer
fewer; fewer
less; less
questions.explanation: The plural count noun requires 'fewer', while the mass noun takes 'less'. Reversing them or applying one form to both ignores the count-versus-quantity distinction.

questions.text: Several investigators evaluating museum admission discounts ___ questioned the original conclusion.
options: has
have
is
was
questions.explanation: Several is a plural quantifier and governs the plural auxiliary have. The singular verbs fail to agree with the head.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 journalism ethics assessment, Either the scholars or the department head ___ required to approve the final summary.
options: were
have
is
are
questions.explanation: The nearest noun head is singular, so is is correct.

questions.text: Which version correctly joins two complete observations about the museum study?
options: The curators recorded entry delays; the elevator was unavailable.
The curators recorded entry delays, the elevator was unavailable.
The curators recorded entry delays; and, the elevator was unavailable.
The curators recorded entry delays: and the elevator was unavailable.
questions.explanation: The semicolon joins two related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction. The comma-only version splices clauses, while the other versions misuse punctuation with 'and'.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 journalism ethics assessment, Which construction uses inversion correctly after the negative adverbial?
options: Not only did the cabinet revise its policy, but it also explained the change.
Not only the cabinet did revise its policy, but explained also.
Not only did the cabinet revised its policy but also explained.
Not only the cabinet had revised its policy, but it also explaining.
questions.explanation: Negative-initial not only requires auxiliary inversion in the first clause.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly identifies the researcher who owns the data table used in the review of museum admission discounts?
options: The researcher who's data table was audited supplied a new copy.
The researcher whose data table was audited supplied a new copy.
The researcher whom's data table was audited supplied a new copy.
The researcher who data table was audited supplied a new copy.
questions.explanation: Whose expresses possession in a relative clause; who's means who is or who has, and the other forms do not serve as possessives.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 journalism ethics assessment, Which sentence means that the director considered just one document and no others?
options: The director only examined the revised summary.
The director examined the only revised summary.
The director examined only the revised summary.
Only the director examined the revised summary.
questions.explanation: Only modifies the immediately following object 'the revised summary' to restrict the documents examined.

The visitor access of the museum study was higher than the prior study.
The visitor access of the museum study was higher than the authors of the prior study.
The visitor access of the museum study was more higher than the prior study.
questions.explanation: 'That of' substitutes for the corresponding measurement in the other project. The distractors compare unlike entities or use an ungrammatical double comparative.

questions.text: The team found a smaller quantity of uncertainty and a smaller number of entry delays. Which sentence describes both changes with appropriate quantifiers?

questions.text: The interviewer asked a neutral question to ___ an honest response.

questions.explanation: Elicit means draw out a response; illicit means unlawful. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

Dr. Ibrahim who inspected the exhibit map, submitted the findings.
Dr. Ibrahim, who inspected the exhibit map submitted the findings.
Dr. Ibrahim who inspected the exhibit map submitted, the findings.
questions.explanation: A supplementary who-clause about an already identified person takes commas on both sides. The other versions omit or misplace a clause boundary.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 journalism ethics assessment, Which version makes the introductory action's agent unambiguous?

Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.

A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 journalism ethics assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?

questions.explanation: The observation alone cannot separate simultaneous causes. The first interpretation preserves the association while recognizing the alternate explanation; the other options infer necessity, absence, or equal effects without evidence.

Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

options: The critic believes every program should be banned permanently.

The critic is opposed to helping the people served by the program.
questions.explanation: The correct response answers the actual causal concern. The alternatives substitute extreme claims about the critic's values or beliefs.

An opinion survey among only those who chose to enroll after the announcement.
A count of project meetings, without any recorded visits by low-income households.
questions.explanation: Outcome measures with appropriate comparison and confounder accounting directly address the alleged improvement. Promotion, selective opinions and meeting totals are weak substitutes for the claimed outcome.

options: Recruit a representative set of users across relevant backgrounds and measure comparable outcomes.
Recruit many more volunteers from the same narrowly selected group.
Ask sponsors to predict how results will generalize.
Assume results generalize because the sample's average improved.

Similarly, the complication proves every finding is false.
Therefore, causal uncertainty can be ignored because the outcome was favorable.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a qualification to favorable evidence and states what remains uncertain. The other transitions turn concurrent changes into unjustified proof.

questions.text: Which revision avoids a dangling participial phrase?

options: is

have
has
questions.explanation: A number of followed by a plural noun takes a plural verb.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Either the inspectors or the department head ___ required to approve the final document.
options: are
were
have
is
questions.explanation: The nearest noun head is singular, so is is correct.

questions.text: Which version correctly joins two complete observations about the newsroom audit?
options: The reporters recorded correction notices, a source recanted.
The reporters recorded correction notices; and, a source recanted.
The reporters recorded correction notices: and a source recanted.
The reporters recorded correction notices; a source recanted.
questions.explanation: The semicolon joins two related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction. The comma-only version splices clauses, while the other versions misuse punctuation with 'and'.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Which construction uses inversion correctly after the negative adverbial?
options: Not only the task force had revised its submission, but it also explaining.
Not only did the task force revise its submission, but it also explained the change.
Not only the task force did revise its submission, but explained also.
Not only did the task force revised its submission but also explained.
questions.explanation: Negative-initial not only requires auxiliary inversion in the first clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Which version uses whose as a relative possessive rather than confusing it with who is?
options: The inspector whose's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The inspector who measurements were disputed requested a review.
The inspector whose measurements were disputed requested a review.
The inspector who's measurements were disputed requested a review.
questions.explanation: Whose is a possessive relative determiner; who's means who is or who has.

questions.text: The review of a newsroom fact-checking policy examined the original dataset and no other dataset. Which sentence expresses the restricted object clearly?
options: Only the analysts examined the original dataset.
The analysts only examined the original dataset.
The analysts examined the only original dataset.
The analysts examined only the original dataset.
questions.explanation: Only directly before the original dataset restricts which material was examined. The other placements change or cloud the scope.

questions.text: A report compares factual accuracy in the newsroom audit and the earlier audit. Which sentence correctly compares the measures rather than a measure with a project?
options: The factual accuracy of the newsroom audit was higher than the earlier audit.
The factual accuracy of the newsroom audit was higher than the authors of the earlier audit.
The factual accuracy of the newsroom audit was more higher than the earlier audit.
The factual accuracy of the newsroom audit was higher than that of the earlier audit.
questions.explanation: 'That of' substitutes for the corresponding measurement in the other project. The distractors compare unlike entities or use an ungrammatical double comparative.

questions.text: The team found a smaller quantity of bias and a smaller number of correction notices. Which sentence describes both changes with appropriate quantifiers?
options: The team recorded fewer bias and less correction notices.
The team recorded less bias and less correction notices.
The team recorded fewer bias and fewer correction notices.
The team recorded less bias and fewer correction notices.
questions.explanation: 'Less' modifies the uncountable quantity and 'fewer' modifies the countable plural. All other combinations misapply at least one quantifier.

questions.text: The reporter ___ beside the witness while listening to the recording.
options: set
sitted
sat
sitting
questions.explanation: Sat is simple past of sit; set means to place an object. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

questions.text: The article briefly ___ to an earlier investigation without naming it.
options: eludes
deludes
intrudes
alludes
questions.explanation: Alludes to means refers indirectly; eludes means escapes. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?
options: The editor said that the task force had reviewed the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the task force will have reviewed the evidence yesterday.
The editor said that the task force review the evidence before it published.
The editor said that the task force had reviews the evidence before publishing.
questions.explanation: Past reporting combines naturally with a past perfect for an earlier action.

questions.text: The report has already identified Ms. Jordan. Which sentence treats the additional information about this named person as nonessential?
options: Ms. Jordan who inspected the editorial system, submitted the findings.
Ms. Jordan, who inspected the editorial system submitted the findings.
Ms. Jordan who inspected the editorial system submitted, the findings.
Ms. Jordan, who inspected the editorial system, submitted the findings.
questions.explanation: A supplementary who-clause about an already identified person takes commas on both sides. The other versions omit or misplace a clause boundary.

questions.text: Which sentence clearly identifies the person who checked the evidence for a newsroom fact-checking policy?
options: After examining the records, the auditors revised their assessment.
After examining the records, the assessment was revised by the auditors.
Examining the records, revisions were made by the auditors.
The revisions, examining the records, were made by the auditors.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase attaches to auditors as the following subject; the alternatives leave the examining action dangling.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Which version appropriately uses were to express an unreal present condition?
options: The task force spoke as if the outcome will already certain.
The task force spoke as if the outcome had certain yesterday.
The task force spoke as if the outcome be already certainty.
The task force spoke as if the outcome were already certain.
questions.explanation: Were marks a contrary-to-fact or hypothetical state in formal usage.

questions.text: Neither of the two interpretations offered for the newsroom audit ___ supported by the available record. Which verb agrees with the singular distributive subject?
options: are
were
have
is
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular in this formal construction, so it takes 'is' rather than a plural verb, regardless of the plural noun in the modifying phrase.

questions.text: Which question uses the formal object pronoun correctly when asking about interviews for a newsroom fact-checking policy?
options: Whom prepared the final review board summary?
Whose did the review board consult about the results?
Who did the review board consult about the results?
Whom did the review board consult about the results?
questions.explanation: Whom is the formal object of did consult. Who is natural in informal speech but the question explicitly asks for formal object case; whom cannot serve as subject.

questions.text: Which version correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause explaining a decision about the newsroom audit?
options: Although a source recanted the reporters, reviewed the evidence.
Although, a source recanted the reporters reviewed the evidence.
Although a source recanted, and the reporters reviewed the evidence.
Although a source recanted, the reporters reviewed the evidence.
questions.explanation: The initial subordinate clause is followed by a comma before the main clause. The other choices misplace the comma or add an ungrammatical conjunction.

questions.text: Which sentence uses parallel objects after 'not only ... but also' when describing the newsroom audit?
options: The reporters examined not only the source notes but also analyzing the published correction.
The reporters examined not only the source notes but also to evaluate the published correction.
The reporters examined not only the source notes but also that the published correction was correct.
The reporters examined not only the source notes but also the published correction.
questions.explanation: Both objects are parallel noun phrases governed by 'examined'. The alternatives shift to a participial, infinitival, or finite clause complement.

questions.text: An essay first describes a popular historical account, then quotes records that contradict its most dramatic detail. What is the strongest description of this structure?
options: Chronological narration followed by an unrelated example.
Definition followed by illustrative classification.
An appeal to popularity that requires no verification.
A received interpretation is introduced and then qualified by contrary primary-source evidence.
questions.explanation: The author contrasts a familiar account with documentary counterevidence, inviting critical revision rather than mere recitation.

questions.text: A safety device completes five demonstrations without failure. Which evidence best supports a reliability estimate for routine industrial use?
options: The designer's confidence in the device.
A shorter demonstration that produces the same result.
A much larger set of representative trials across expected operating stresses with recorded failures.
The absence of complaints during the five demonstrations.
questions.explanation: Reliability requires sufficient trials under relevant stresses and explicit failure tracking, not just a handful of successes.

questions.text: A proposal to expand a newsroom fact-checking policy faces this objection: verification can delay publication. Which response keeps a defensible argument without dismissing the concern?
options: The expense matters, but a newsroom fact-checking policy has already been discussed widely enough that measuring outcomes is unnecessary.
Because the program is intended to help, its costs and risks should not be weighed in the decision.
The concern could be reduced by delaying the decision, even if the program's effect on the rate of corrected factual errors is never measured.
Although verification can delay publication, a restricted pilot that measures the rate of corrected factual errors could show whether expansion is justified.
questions.explanation: The strongest response acknowledges the specific burden while proposing evidence about the rate of corrected factual errors. The alternatives appeal to publicity, intentions, or postponement without addressing effectiveness and cost together.

questions.text: In the day 10 museum conservation full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in museum conservation?
options: Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: A paragraph reports encouraging initial results for a newsroom fact-checking policy. The next explains that the newspaper published fewer investigative articles. Which transition and qualification best connect the paragraphs?
options: Furthermore, the timing of the competing change demonstrates that the new program produced the entire benefit.
Nevertheless, the newspaper published fewer investigative articles, so the effect of the program itself remains uncertain.
By contrast, the competing change establishes that the program had no effect at all.
Consequently, additional evidence is unnecessary because both changes occurred in the same period.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' marks a limitation to positive findings and preserves uncertainty about the competing change. The other options assert proof of benefit or ineffectiveness or dismiss the need for comparison.

questions.text: In the day 10 museum conservation full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in museum conservation?
options: The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?
options: The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
All respondents prefer answering surveys.
The survey document contains at least two paragraphs.
The inspectors interviewed every official.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: Observed the rate of corrected factual errors changed after a newsroom fact-checking policy began. At the same time, the newspaper published fewer investigative articles. Which interpretation avoids a post hoc fallacy?
options: Any favorable change following the launch must have resulted from the program.
The concurrent change proves the program was irrelevant in every setting.
The timing is compatible with an effect, but it cannot isolate the program from the concurrent change.
Since both changes occurred together, they must have had exactly equal effects.
questions.explanation: The observation alone cannot separate simultaneous causes. The first interpretation preserves the association while recognizing the alternate explanation; the other options infer necessity, absence, or equal effects without evidence.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
The cost is irrelevant because the submission is well intentioned.
Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Which sentence avoids a straw-man response?
options: The critic believes no data should ever be collected.
The critic must oppose every form of scientific inquiry.
The objection is false because the critic sounds worried.
The objection concerns uncertainty in the sample, which the next review should directly address.
questions.explanation: A fair rebuttal answers the actual concern about sampling rather than misrepresenting it as total opposition.

questions.text: A council attributes changes in the rate of corrected factual errors to a newsroom fact-checking policy. Which evidence would most directly evaluate this causal claim?
options: The number of promotional materials distributed when the project started.
An opinion survey among only those who chose to enroll after the announcement.
A count of project meetings, without any recorded the rate of corrected factual errors.
Comparable before-and-after outcome measures, with baseline differences and the newspaper published fewer investigative articles accounted for.
questions.explanation: Outcome measures with appropriate comparison and confounder accounting directly address the alleged improvement. Promotion, selective opinions and meeting totals are weak substitutes for the claimed outcome.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: Removing participants who disagree with the inspector's conclusion.
Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
A larger poster advertising the first trial.
An additional summary of the same initial observations.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 engineering safety assessment, Which transition links a paragraph of favorable evidence to a paragraph about its limits?
options: For instance, the first result proves every outcome.
Likewise, no further evidence is needed.
Nevertheless, the review's restricted time frame prevents stronger conclusions.
Consequently, all uncertainty has disappeared.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals a contrast between encouraging findings and a meaningful qualification.

questions.text: A student is writing a policy essay about a newsroom fact-checking policy. Which thesis is both contestable and specific enough to evaluate?
options: A limited expansion should be considered if measured gains in the rate of corrected factual errors justify costs after accounting for competing explanations.
There are many views about the program, some supportive and some critical.
This essay will discuss several possible aspects of the proposed program.
The program is good because well-intentioned people have recommended it.
questions.explanation: The first thesis advocates a concrete conditional policy grounded in outcomes and costs. The other statements merely announce a topic, summarize opinions, or rely on intentions rather than evaluable reasoning.

questions.text: Two explanations fit an observed shift in the rate of corrected factual errors: the launch of a newsroom fact-checking policy and the fact that the newspaper published fewer investigative articles. Which next measurement best distinguishes them?
options: Collect additional testimonials from people who already believe the program worked.
Repeat the preferred explanation in the report's conclusion.
Measure the launch date more precisely without collecting any outcome data.
Compare similar groups with differing exposure to the program while measuring the competing change.
questions.explanation: A comparison varying exposure while tracking the rival factor tests divergent causal predictions. Testimonials, repetition and precise launch dates alone do not discriminate explanations.

questions.text: A review seeks to estimate whether a newsroom fact-checking policy altered the rate of corrected factual errors. Which approach supplies the most defensible counterfactual?
options: Compare the participants' comments only after the program has ended.
Use the program's stated objective as evidence that it reached that objective.
Compare suitably matched participants or sites with and without the program, adjusting for baseline outcome differences.
Measure only the most successful pilot site and generalize to every site.
questions.explanation: A matched comparison with baseline adjustment can approximate what would have happened without the intervention. Selection based on success and opinions or intentions cannot establish the counterfactual.

questions.text: A sponsor claims a newsroom fact-checking policy produced a lasting improvement in the rate of corrected factual errors. Which assessment most fairly evaluates the sponsor's evidence?
options: Accept the claim if the sponsor has a prestigious professional title.
Inspect the sampling method, underlying outcome data, and independent replication while checking the competing change.
Reject the claim without examination because the source has a financial interest.
Count how many different websites repeat the sponsor's press release.
questions.explanation: Evaluating methods, records and independent evidence addresses both credibility and possible bias. Reputation, automatic dismissal, and repetitive citation alone are not sufficient tests.

questions.text: An archived local report describes a newsroom fact-checking policy at one site in a particular year. Which historical inference is warranted without additional records?
options: The program was documented at that site, but its prevalence or effects elsewhere remain uncertain.
The program must have been identical at every institution in the country.
The archived description proves every participant supported the program.
The presence of one report establishes its effectiveness throughout the entire period.
questions.explanation: One record can document existence in its own context but cannot establish geographic prevalence, universal attitudes, or effectiveness without corroboration.

questions.text: A writer compares an initial pilot of a newsroom fact-checking policy with a trial of a new school schedule. When would the analogy offer meaningful evidence for expansion?
options: When both initiatives were announced in the same season, regardless of their mechanisms.
When their titles sound similar even if the intended users differ.
When the school trial was popular, even if it never measured any outcome.
When both pilots share relevant constraints, comparable target groups, and outcomes measured against plausible alternatives.
questions.explanation: Analogies support inference when the features bearing on the conclusion are shared. Superficial timing, naming, and popularity do not establish comparable mechanisms or outcomes.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in the rate of corrected factual errors but cannot separate a newsroom fact-checking policy from the competing circumstance that the newspaper published fewer investigative articles. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?
options: The positive change proves that every participant benefited exclusively from the program.
The competing circumstance disproves the existence of any possible program benefit.
The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly treats the date as additional information rather than as a restrictive condition?
options: The report, which was published in October, contradicted the earlier forecast.
The report which was published in October, contradicted the earlier forecast.
The report, which was published in October contradicted the earlier forecast.
The report which, was published in October, contradicted the earlier forecast.
questions.explanation: The paired commas set off a nonrestrictive relative clause. The other versions contain mismatched commas.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: Each of the findings that the writers discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: If Priya ___ responsible for the draft, the chair would seek independent confirmation.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: The draft may be accepted only if the writers approve it. What can be inferred?

Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
Their approval guarantees acceptance.
Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Priya as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After she inspected it, Priya informed the chair.
The chair and Priya discussed the findings after she inspected it.
After inspecting the evidence, Priya informed the chair.
Priya informed the chair after she inspected it.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'After inspecting the evidence' directly modifies the named person who performed the inspection. The alternatives contain ambiguous pronouns or less clearly attach the action to its agent.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: Which sentence means that the writers revised no section except the conclusion?
options: Only the writers revised the conclusion of the draft.
The writers only revised the conclusion of the draft.
The writers revised the only conclusion of the draft.
The writers revised only the conclusion of the draft.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The draft was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The draft was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The draft was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
The draft was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: The number of writers assigned to the task ___ increased since September.

questions.text: The revised irrigation plan showed a decline in the number of pump failures but also in the amount of runoff. Which pair of quantifiers correctly completes the sentence: 'There were ___ pump failures and ___ runoff'?

The water efficiency of the irrigation trial was more higher than the earlier trial.

Dr. Hayes, who inspected the flow meter, submitted the findings.
Dr. Hayes who inspected the flow meter submitted, the findings.

questions.text: One school's average score rose while its median remained unchanged. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Every student's score increased.
At least one score changed enough to affect the mean, but the median alone does not determine how the distribution shifted.
The middle-ranked student's score must have decreased.
The change proves a recording error.
questions.explanation: A changed mean alongside an unchanged median is compatible with multiple distributions; it does not describe each person's trajectory.

questions.text: A historian infers that crop prices caused rural migration because prices fell before a migration wave. What would most strengthen the causal argument?
options: Regional evidence linking price changes to household departures while assessing simultaneous political or environmental pressures.
A later novel depicting a migrating family.
A local song remembering economic hardship.
Proof that crops were grown in the region.
questions.explanation: Linked region-level or household evidence and consideration of rival pressures distinguish mere timing from explanatory mechanism.

questions.text: A proposal to expand a farm irrigation pilot faces this objection: irrigation equipment is expensive to maintain. Which response keeps a defensible argument without dismissing the concern?
options: The expense matters, but a farm irrigation pilot has already been discussed widely enough that measuring outcomes is unnecessary.
Because the program is intended to help, its costs and risks should not be weighed in the decision.
Although irrigation equipment is expensive to maintain, a restricted pilot that measures crop yield per unit of water could show whether expansion is justified.
The concern could be reduced by delaying the decision, even if the program's effect on crop yield per unit of water is never measured.
questions.explanation: The strongest response acknowledges the specific burden while proposing evidence about crop yield per unit of water. The alternatives appeal to publicity, intentions, or postponement without addressing effectiveness and cost together.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in medical history?
options: Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: A paragraph reports encouraging initial results for a farm irrigation pilot. The next explains that fertilizer use also increased. Which transition and qualification best connect the paragraphs?
options: Nevertheless, fertilizer use also increased, so the effect of the program itself remains uncertain.
Furthermore, the timing of the competing change demonstrates that the new program produced the entire benefit.
By contrast, the competing change establishes that the program had no effect at all.
Consequently, additional evidence is unnecessary because both changes occurred in the same period.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' marks a limitation to positive findings and preserves uncertainty about the competing change. The other options assert proof of benefit or ineffectiveness or dismiss the need for comparison.

questions.text: In the day 11 medical history full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in medical history?
options: An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 agricultural history assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?
options: The writers interviewed every official.
The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
All respondents prefer answering surveys.
The survey draft contains at least two paragraphs.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: Observed crop yield per unit of water changed after a farm irrigation pilot began. At the same time, fertilizer use also increased. Which interpretation avoids a post hoc fallacy?
options: Any favorable change following the launch must have resulted from the program.
The timing is compatible with an effect, but it cannot isolate the program from the concurrent change.
The concurrent change proves the program was irrelevant in every setting.
Since both changes occurred together, they must have had exactly equal effects.
questions.explanation: The observation alone cannot separate simultaneous causes. The first interpretation preserves the association while recognizing the alternate explanation; the other options infer necessity, absence, or equal effects without evidence.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 agricultural history assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
The cost is irrelevant because the proposal is well intentioned.
Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 agricultural history assessment, Which sentence avoids a straw-man response?
options: The objection concerns uncertainty in the sample, which the next study should directly address.
The critic believes no data should ever be collected.
The critic must oppose every form of scientific inquiry.
The objection is false because the critic sounds worried.
questions.explanation: A fair rebuttal answers the actual concern about sampling rather than misrepresenting it as total opposition.

questions.text: A council attributes changes in crop yield per unit of water to a farm irrigation pilot. Which evidence would most directly evaluate this causal claim?
options: The number of promotional materials distributed when the project started.
An opinion survey among only those who chose to enroll after the announcement.
Comparable before-and-after outcome measures, with baseline differences and fertilizer use also increased accounted for.
A count of project meetings, without any recorded crop yield per unit of water.
questions.explanation: Outcome measures with appropriate comparison and confounder accounting directly address the alleged improvement. Promotion, selective opinions and meeting totals are weak substitutes for the claimed outcome.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 agricultural history assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: An additional summary of the same initial observations.
Removing participants who disagree with the writer's conclusion.
Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
A larger poster advertising the first trial.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 agricultural history assessment, Which transition links a paragraph of favorable evidence to a paragraph about its limits?
options: Consequently, all uncertainty has disappeared.
For instance, the first result proves every outcome.
Likewise, no further evidence is needed.
Nevertheless, the study's restricted time frame prevents stronger conclusions.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals a contrast between encouraging findings and a meaningful qualification.

questions.text: A student is writing a policy essay about a farm irrigation pilot. Which thesis is both contestable and specific enough to evaluate?
options: There are many views about the program, some supportive and some critical.
This essay will discuss several possible aspects of the proposed program.
The program is good because well-intentioned people have recommended it.
A limited expansion should be considered if measured gains in crop yield per unit of water justify costs after accounting for competing explanations.
questions.explanation: The first thesis advocates a concrete conditional policy grounded in outcomes and costs. The other statements merely announce a topic, summarize opinions, or rely on intentions rather than evaluable reasoning.

questions.text: Two explanations fit an observed shift in crop yield per unit of water: the launch of a farm irrigation pilot and the fact that fertilizer use also increased. Which next measurement best distinguishes them?
options: Collect additional testimonials from people who already believe the program worked.
Repeat the preferred explanation in the report's conclusion.
Compare similar groups with differing exposure to the program while measuring the competing change.
Measure the launch date more precisely without collecting any outcome data.
questions.explanation: A comparison varying exposure while tracking the rival factor tests divergent causal predictions. Testimonials, repetition and precise launch dates alone do not discriminate explanations.

questions.text: A review seeks to estimate whether a farm irrigation pilot altered crop yield per unit of water. Which approach supplies the most defensible counterfactual?
options: Compare the participants' comments only after the program has ended.
Compare suitably matched participants or sites with and without the program, adjusting for baseline outcome differences.
Use the program's stated objective as evidence that it reached that objective.
Measure only the most successful pilot site and generalize to every site.
questions.explanation: A matched comparison with baseline adjustment can approximate what would have happened without the intervention. Selection based on success and opinions or intentions cannot establish the counterfactual.

questions.text: A sponsor claims a farm irrigation pilot produced a lasting improvement in crop yield per unit of water. Which assessment most fairly evaluates the sponsor's evidence?
options: Inspect the sampling method, underlying outcome data, and independent replication while checking the competing change.
Accept the claim if the sponsor has a prestigious professional title.
Reject the claim without examination because the source has a financial interest.
Count how many different websites repeat the sponsor's press release.
questions.explanation: Evaluating methods, records and independent evidence addresses both credibility and possible bias. Reputation, automatic dismissal, and repetitive citation alone are not sufficient tests.

questions.text: An archived local report describes a farm irrigation pilot at one site in a particular year. Which historical inference is warranted without additional records?
options: The program must have been identical at every institution in the country.
The archived description proves every participant supported the program.
The presence of one report establishes its effectiveness throughout the entire period.
The program was documented at that site, but its prevalence or effects elsewhere remain uncertain.
questions.explanation: One record can document existence in its own context but cannot establish geographic prevalence, universal attitudes, or effectiveness without corroboration.

questions.text: A writer compares an initial pilot of a farm irrigation pilot with a trial of a new school schedule. When would the analogy offer meaningful evidence for expansion?
options: When both initiatives were announced in the same season, regardless of their mechanisms.
When their titles sound similar even if the intended users differ.
When both pilots share relevant constraints, comparable target groups, and outcomes measured against plausible alternatives.
When the school trial was popular, even if it never measured any outcome.
questions.explanation: Analogies support inference when the features bearing on the conclusion are shared. Superficial timing, naming, and popularity do not establish comparable mechanisms or outcomes.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in crop yield per unit of water but cannot separate a farm irrigation pilot from the competing circumstance that fertilizer use also increased. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?
options: The positive change proves that every participant benefited exclusively from the program.
The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
The competing circumstance disproves the existence of any possible program benefit.
No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly handles subject–verb agreement after an introductory locative phrase?
options: Among the exhibits was several letters whose dates were uncertain.
Among the exhibits were several letters whose dates were uncertain.
Among the exhibits were several letters whose dates was uncertain.
Among the exhibits had been several letters whose dates is uncertain.
questions.explanation: The inverted subject 'several letters' is plural and takes 'were'; the relative clause's plural 'dates' also takes 'were'.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: Each of the findings that the analysts discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.
options: have been
is
are
were
questions.explanation: The singular distributive head each governs is despite the intervening plural phrase.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: By the time Jules presented the record, the review team ___ its sources.
options: will check
is checking
had already checked
has already checked
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.
options: a discrepancy became apparent
the record was amended
the result seemed doubtful
the analysts revised their interpretation
questions.explanation: The people who performed the reviewing must immediately follow the opening modifier.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.
options: that in the earlier record
the previous chair
the original analysts
the archive that stored the document
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: If Jules ___ responsible for the record, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: is
were
will be
has been
questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: The record may be accepted only if the analysts approve it. What can be inferred?
options: Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
No unapproved amendment has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
Their approval guarantees acceptance.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Jules as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: Jules informed the chair after she inspected it.
After she inspected it, Jules informed the chair.
The chair and Jules discussed the findings after she inspected it.
After inspecting the evidence, Jules informed the chair.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'After inspecting the evidence' directly modifies the named person who performed the inspection. The alternatives contain ambiguous pronouns or less clearly attach the action to its agent.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: Which sentence means that the analysts revised no section except the conclusion?
options: The analysts revised only the conclusion of the record.
Only the analysts revised the conclusion of the record.
The analysts only revised the conclusion of the record.
The analysts revised the only conclusion of the record.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The record was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
The record was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The record was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The record was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 12 economics full-paper case: The number of analysts assigned to the task ___ increased since September.
options: were
are
has
have
questions.explanation: The singular head number takes has, despite the plural noun in its complement.

questions.text: The revised subsidy assessment showed a decline in the number of eviction notices but also in the amount of uncertainty. Which pair of quantifiers correctly completes the sentence: 'There were ___ eviction notices and ___ uncertainty'?
options: less; fewer
fewer; less
fewer; fewer
less; less
questions.explanation: The plural count noun requires 'fewer', while the mass noun takes 'less'. Reversing them or applying one form to both ignores the count-versus-quantity distinction.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, A number of researchers ___ raised concerns about the proposed interpretation.
options: have
has
is
was
questions.explanation: A number of followed by a plural noun takes a plural verb.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Either the analysts or the department head ___ required to approve the final record.
options: have

are
were
questions.explanation: The nearest noun head is singular, so is is correct.

questions.text: Which version correctly joins two complete observations about the housing analysis?
options: The economists recorded eviction notices, a landlord changed rents.
The economists recorded eviction notices; a landlord changed rents.
The economists recorded eviction notices; and, a landlord changed rents.
The economists recorded eviction notices: and a landlord changed rents.
questions.explanation: The semicolon joins two related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction. The comma-only version splices clauses, while the other versions misuse punctuation with 'and'.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Which construction uses inversion correctly after the negative adverbial?
options: Not only the review board did revise its amendment, but explained also.
Not only did the review board revised its amendment but also explained.
Not only the review board had revised its amendment, but it also explaining.
Not only did the review board revise its amendment, but it also explained the change.
questions.explanation: Negative-initial not only requires auxiliary inversion in the first clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Which version uses whose as a relative possessive rather than confusing it with who is?
options: The researcher whose measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher who's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher whose's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher who measurements were disputed requested a review.
questions.explanation: Whose is a possessive relative determiner; who's means who is or who has.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Which sentence means that the director considered just one document and no others?
options: The director examined the only revised record.
The director examined only the revised record.
Only the director examined the revised record.
The director only examined the revised record.
questions.explanation: Only modifies the immediately following object 'the revised record' to restrict the documents examined.

questions.text: A report compares tenant stability in the housing analysis and the prior analysis. Which sentence correctly compares the measures rather than a measure with a project?
options: The tenant stability of the housing analysis was higher than the prior analysis.
The tenant stability of the housing analysis was higher than that of the prior analysis.
The tenant stability of the housing analysis was higher than the authors of the prior analysis.
The tenant stability of the housing analysis was more higher than the prior analysis.
questions.explanation: 'That of' substitutes for the corresponding measurement in the other project. The distractors compare unlike entities or use an ungrammatical double comparative.

questions.text: The team found a smaller quantity of uncertainty and a smaller number of eviction notices. Which sentence describes both changes with appropriate quantifiers?
options: The team recorded fewer uncertainty and less eviction notices.
The team recorded less uncertainty and fewer eviction notices.
The team recorded less uncertainty and less eviction notices.
The team recorded fewer uncertainty and fewer eviction notices.
questions.explanation: 'Less' modifies the uncountable quantity and 'fewer' modifies the countable plural. All other combinations misapply at least one quantifier.

questions.text: The signed lease had ___ in the folder for weeks.
options: lain
laid
lay
lied
questions.explanation: Had lain is the past perfect of intransitive lie; laid is transitive. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

questions.text: The housing survey ___ the council vote by two weeks.
options: proceeded
preceded
preceding
proceed
questions.explanation: Preceded means occurred before; proceeded means continued. Other choices have an incorrect form, meaning, or syntactic role in this context.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?
options: The editor said that the review board review the evidence before it published.
The editor said that the review board had reviews the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the review board had reviewed the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the review board will have reviewed the evidence yesterday.
questions.explanation: Past reporting combines naturally with a past perfect for an earlier action.

questions.text: The report has already identified Ms. Reed. Which sentence treats the additional information about this named person as nonessential?
options: Ms. Reed who inspected the rent database, submitted the findings.
Ms. Reed, who inspected the rent database, submitted the findings.
Ms. Reed, who inspected the rent database submitted the findings.
Ms. Reed who inspected the rent database submitted, the findings.
questions.explanation: A supplementary who-clause about an already identified person takes commas on both sides. The other versions omit or misplace a clause boundary.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Which version makes the introductory action's agent unambiguous?
options: Having reviewed the transcript, the historian corrected the chronology.
Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.
After studying the archive, a discrepancy appeared.
Having read the transcript, the record's conclusions changed.
questions.explanation: The historian is the following subject and therefore performs the reviewing.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Which version appropriately uses were to express an unreal present condition?
options: The review board spoke as if the outcome be already certainty.
The review board spoke as if the outcome were already certain.
The review board spoke as if the outcome will already certain.
The review board spoke as if the outcome had certain yesterday.
questions.explanation: Were marks a contrary-to-fact or hypothetical state in formal usage.

questions.text: Neither of the two interpretations offered for the housing analysis ___ supported by the available record. Which verb agrees with the singular distributive subject?
options: are
is
were
have
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular in this formal construction, so it takes 'is' rather than a plural verb, regardless of the plural noun in the modifying phrase.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, Which question correctly uses whom in a formal object position?
options: Whom submitted the final record?
Whom was responsible for the analysis?
Whom have been approved for the hearing?
Whom did the panel invite to testify?
questions.explanation: Whom is the object of invite; the other questions need subject-case who.

questions.text: Which version correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause explaining a decision about the housing analysis?
options: Although a landlord changed rents the economists, reviewed the evidence.
Although a landlord changed rents, the economists reviewed the evidence.
Although, a landlord changed rents the economists reviewed the evidence.
Although a landlord changed rents, and the economists reviewed the evidence.
questions.explanation: The initial subordinate clause is followed by a comma before the main clause. The other choices misplace the comma or add an ungrammatical conjunction.

questions.text: Which sentence uses parallel objects after 'not only ... but also' when describing the housing analysis?
options: The economists examined not only the lease records but also analyzing the subsidy assessment.
The economists examined not only the lease records but also the subsidy assessment.
The economists examined not only the lease records but also to evaluate the subsidy assessment.
The economists examined not only the lease records but also that the subsidy assessment was correct.
questions.explanation: Both objects are parallel noun phrases governed by 'examined'. The alternatives shift to a participial, infinitival, or finite clause complement.

questions.text: An experiment showed no statistically detectable difference between two treatments in a small sample. Which formulation is most responsible?

The treatment selected first must be more effective.
questions.explanation: Failure to detect a difference does not prove equivalence, especially when the study may lack power.

questions.text: A national survey's responses increased after a redesigned online form. What measure best indicates whether the change improved representation rather than only participation volume?

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 social statistics assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: A larger poster advertising the first trial.
An additional summary of the same initial observations.
Removing participants who disagree with the researcher's conclusion.
Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: One paragraph reports encouraging changes in households avoiding eviction; the next considers regional rents declined temporarily. Which opening makes the relationship clear?
options: Nevertheless, the competing circumstance limits any immediate claim that the program alone caused the improvement.
Furthermore, the competing circumstance demonstrates the program was the sole cause.
Similarly, the complication proves every finding is false.
Therefore, causal uncertainty can be ignored because the outcome was favorable.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a qualification to favorable evidence and states what remains uncertain. The other transitions turn concurrent changes into unjustified proof.

questions.text: A student is writing a policy essay about housing rent-support vouchers. Which thesis is both contestable and specific enough to evaluate?
options: There are many views about the program, some supportive and some critical.
This essay will discuss several possible aspects of the proposed program.
A limited expansion should be considered if measured gains in households avoiding eviction justify costs after accounting for competing explanations.
The program is good because well-intentioned people have recommended it.
questions.explanation: The first thesis advocates a concrete conditional policy grounded in outcomes and costs. The other statements merely announce a topic, summarize opinions, or rely on intentions rather than evaluable reasoning.

questions.text: Two explanations fit an observed shift in households avoiding eviction: the launch of housing rent-support vouchers and the fact that regional rents declined temporarily. Which next measurement best distinguishes them?
options: Collect additional testimonials from people who already believe the program worked.
Compare similar groups with differing exposure to the program while measuring the competing change.
Repeat the preferred explanation in the report's conclusion.
Measure the launch date more precisely without collecting any outcome data.
questions.explanation: A comparison varying exposure while tracking the rival factor tests divergent causal predictions. Testimonials, repetition and precise launch dates alone do not discriminate explanations.

questions.text: A review seeks to estimate whether housing rent-support vouchers altered households avoiding eviction. Which approach supplies the most defensible counterfactual?
options: Compare suitably matched participants or sites with and without the program, adjusting for baseline outcome differences.
Compare the participants' comments only after the program has ended.
Use the program's stated objective as evidence that it reached that objective.
Measure only the most successful pilot site and generalize to every site.
questions.explanation: A matched comparison with baseline adjustment can approximate what would have happened without the intervention. Selection based on success and opinions or intentions cannot establish the counterfactual.

questions.text: A sponsor claims housing rent-support vouchers produced a lasting improvement in households avoiding eviction. Which assessment most fairly evaluates the sponsor's evidence?
options: Accept the claim if the sponsor has a prestigious professional title.
Reject the claim without examination because the source has a financial interest.
Count how many different websites repeat the sponsor's press release.
Inspect the sampling method, underlying outcome data, and independent replication while checking the competing change.
questions.explanation: Evaluating methods, records and independent evidence addresses both credibility and possible bias. Reputation, automatic dismissal, and repetitive citation alone are not sufficient tests.

questions.text: An archived local report describes housing rent-support vouchers at one site in a particular year. Which historical inference is warranted without additional records?
options: The program must have been identical at every institution in the country.
The archived description proves every participant supported the program.
The program was documented at that site, but its prevalence or effects elsewhere remain uncertain.
The presence of one report establishes its effectiveness throughout the entire period.
questions.explanation: One record can document existence in its own context but cannot establish geographic prevalence, universal attitudes, or effectiveness without corroboration.

questions.text: A writer compares an initial pilot of housing rent-support vouchers with a trial of a new school schedule. When would the analogy offer meaningful evidence for expansion?
options: When both initiatives were announced in the same season, regardless of their mechanisms.
When both pilots share relevant constraints, comparable target groups, and outcomes measured against plausible alternatives.
When their titles sound similar even if the intended users differ.
When the school trial was popular, even if it never measured any outcome.
questions.explanation: Analogies support inference when the features bearing on the conclusion are shared. Superficial timing, naming, and popularity do not establish comparable mechanisms or outcomes.

questions.text: A report identifies an encouraging change in households avoiding eviction but cannot separate housing rent-support vouchers from the competing circumstance that regional rents declined temporarily. Which conclusion best synthesizes the evidence?
options: The observations justify targeted follow-up, but a program-specific causal benefit remains unconfirmed.
The positive change proves that every participant benefited exclusively from the program.
The competing circumstance disproves the existence of any possible program benefit.
No preliminary description of the outcome is permissible while uncertainty remains.
questions.explanation: The first synthesis reports the observation and a reasonable next step while retaining causal uncertainty. The alternatives overgeneralize, deny possible effects, or refuse to describe valid limited evidence.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly distinguishes the group considered as a whole from its individual participants?
options: Each of the participants have submitted their observations.
Each of the participants were submitting their observations.
Each of the participants has submitted their observations.
Each of the participants are submitting their observations.
questions.explanation: The distributive subject 'each' takes a singular finite verb, 'has'; singular 'their' is accepted for a person of unspecified gender.

questions.text: Each of the analysts who evaluated a classroom robotics program ___ responsible for a separate written report. Choose the formal singular verb.
options: is
are
have
were
questions.explanation: Each is the singular grammatical head and takes is despite plural analysts in the intervening phrase.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: By the time Mira presented the proposal, the review team ___ its sources.
options: has already checked
will check
is checking
had already checked
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.
options: the surveyors revised their interpretation
a discrepancy became apparent
the proposal was amended
the result seemed doubtful
questions.explanation: The people who performed the reviewing must immediately follow the opening modifier.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.
options: the archive that stored the document
that in the earlier proposal
the previous chair
the original surveyors
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: If Mira ___ responsible for the proposal, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: has been
is
were
will be
questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: The proposal may be accepted only if the surveyors approve it. What can be inferred?
options: Their approval guarantees acceptance.
Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
No unapproved motion has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Mira as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After inspecting the evidence, Mira informed the chair.
Mira informed the chair after she inspected it.
After she inspected it, Mira informed the chair.
The chair and Mira discussed the findings after she inspected it.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'After inspecting the evidence' directly modifies the named person who performed the inspection. The alternatives contain ambiguous pronouns or less clearly attach the action to its agent.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: Which sentence means that the surveyors revised no section except the conclusion?
options: The surveyors revised the only conclusion of the proposal.
The surveyors revised only the conclusion of the proposal.
Only the surveyors revised the conclusion of the proposal.
The surveyors only revised the conclusion of the proposal.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 13 marine science full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
